label: early original-phase steps (t=2-5) just after a d (also f/c/u)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase at steps t=2-5 (peak t=3; essentially never at t<2, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase). Within that window it is driven by which tokens appeared one or two steps earlier: d is by far the strongest (prev_tok=d 12x lift, ~46% of mass), then f, c, u, a, v. The current token modulates it too (d, c, l, w, v, n strongest) and first occurrences of a token fire more than repeats. Fewer digits in the sequence means more firing. The biggest activations come on d d / x d d prefixes followed by d, c, or a new letter at t=3. It looks like a graded, roughly additive mix of these token contributions, not a crisp rule. A position-window plus recent-d/f/c/u predicate catches 95% of the mass but only 13% precision; the recorded d-specific predicate trades recall for precision (dev P 0.30, R 0.48, mass 0.58).
